_comment: Byte ceiling and parser cap for the self-hosted hook bundle (dist/hooks/dispatch.js). Registered by road-to-a-hook-bundle-with-one-yaml-reader step 2.1. Read by src/scripts/check_hook_bundle_composition.ts, which builds the bundle from source with --metafile and compares. WHY A CEILING AT ALL: every concern is inlined into one bundle that every hook event loads, so a dependency added for one concern is paid by all of them, on every dispatch. The second YAML parser that opened this roadmap cost 95,846 bytes and reached a release as a review finding rather than as a red check. A ceiling makes the next one a red check.
max_bytes_derivation: Measured 1,514,715 bytes on origin/main at 213d87055 (the gate's own reading, APFS-cloned node_modules so no worktree path artefacts). The ceiling is that reading plus ~2.3 % of headroom, rounded to 1,550,000, on the same doctrine as the 2026-10-01 registration: a bundle is rebuilt from source on every run, so an esbuild minor that renames symbols moves the figure by hundreds of bytes with no change to this tree, and a ceiling one byte above the reading would red on that. Composition is healthy at this reading and was checked rather than assumed: one YAML package (258,833 bytes) and 1,238,525 bytes of own source, so the growth is own code, not a re-entered dependency. The 1,564,211-byte pre-swap regression this roadmap closed still cannot reappear under it. RAISED to 1,550,500 on 2026-10-23 for the InstructionsLoaded binding (237 bytes against 51 of headroom); the reasoning and the measured alternative are the last `raise_log` entry, so this paragraph describes the 1,550,000 registration and the raise is recorded there rather than restated.
shrink_only_note: A RAISE needs a recorded reason in `raise_log` below naming what was added and why it could not be avoided. Enforced since road-to-a-ratification-fence-that-follows-its-imports 3.2: the gate reads `max_bytes` at the base revision, and a working value above it fails unless `raise_log` gained an entry whose `to` equals the new value. A lowering needs no entry. This file is also on the ratification gate's watched set, so a raise carries a record as well as a log entry.

raise_log.what_was_added: Nothing in this commit. The 1,500,000 ceiling was red on the very commit that registered it: measured 1,511,489 bytes at 22b19e520, which is the merge of the PR that introduced the budget. Its derivation read 1,469,738 bytes on the PR branch, whose base predated three PRs that had merged meanwhile — the failure-event binding of #2160 (sixteen concerns on a new slot), the touched-file quality pass of #2152, and the evidence classification of #2153 — and #2162 landed after it. The gate ran on each PR's pre-merge tree and never on the merge result, so every one of those PRs was green alone and the trunk was red the moment they were together.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: The bytes are deliberately merged capability, not an accident to trim: the composition check above shows one parser and no duplicate dependency, so there is nothing to remove that would not remove a feature. The alternative — reverting a merged lane to fit a ceiling derived against a base that no longer exists — would discard working code to satisfy a number that never described this tree.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Measuring the ceiling against the merge result rather than the PR branch. A ceiling derived on a branch is a statement about that branch; the trunk is what the gate defends, and the two diverge exactly when several lanes land in one day.

raise_log.what_was_added: The queued engine work the 28,000 ceiling was sized for, landed together: the validated identifier rows of one-detector 2.3 (IBAN, card, e-mail with a keyed-digest allowlist, three phone shapes, German tax id, US SSN), and three free-tier credential rows (Hugging Face, NVIDIA, Replicate) of free-hands 1.2. The invisible-character normalisation of one-detector 2.5 (`egress_normalize.ts`) is not in this chunk: the engine does not import it (corrected 2026-10-23, road-to-a-tick-the-shipped-path-earns 1.4). Measured 30,445 bytes when the raise landed; 30,493 bytes at the ratified revision, after the round-6 IBAN rows.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: Each addition is an identifier or credential detection row; the 2026-10-18 derivation already counted them as the chunk's planned growth and underestimated their sum by about 2.4 KB. The chunk is loaded only when a caller needs detection, so no dispatch pays these bytes; the dispatch bundle itself is unchanged.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Re-measuring the queued items' sum when the ceiling was set, rather than estimating each.

raise_log.what_was_added: The `InstructionsLoaded` binding: one `LAZY_CONCERNS` row for the observer (its 11,097-byte body ships in its own chunk, never in this bundle) and the event name in the three vocabularies the bundle carries (dispatcher, collector, journal). Measured 1,550,186 bytes with the binding by the gate; the same esbuild invocation on the base and on this branch differs by 237 bytes, so the base sat at 1,549,949 — 51 bytes of headroom.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: D8 (council, 2026-10-18) asked for room before a raise. Room was tried and measured: moving `session-eol` (27,708 B in-bundle, `stop` alone) into a chunk freed 29,948 B (same esbuild invocation, with and without the move) but produced a 259,330-byte chunk (`yaml` external) required on every `stop` — about 8.5 times the bytes that event parses today, to buy 186. The observer itself was already moved out. What remains in the bundle is the row and three event-name strings, which no chunk can carry.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the base sat 51 bytes under the ceiling, so any new event in the vocabulary would have tripped it. Sized to this binding plus about 300 bytes; step 3.3's promotion is sized when it is built.

chunks.derivation: Measured 60,718 bytes on 2026-10-18, the SVG rule set the council moved out of the dispatch bundle on 2026-10-11. Registered when the composition gate began requiring a ceiling for every defined chunk (council round 4b, 2026-10-18), so a chunk added to hook_chunks.mjs cannot ship unmeasured. The ceiling is that reading plus about 5 %, rounded, with no growth queued for it.

Measured 18,478 bytes on 2026-10-18 (the rule table, the token grammar and the commit scanner, with the per-rule linearity prose moved to a test-only module). The ceiling is that reading plus the queued engine work of road-to-one-detector-and-the-senders-we-own (validated identifier rules about 4.3 KB, known values, the invisible-character rescan and the variant suffix about 1-2 KB each), rounded up. An AI council of two providers chose on 2026-10-18 to move the engine out of the dispatch bundle into this conditional chunk rather than raise the dispatch ceiling, and asked that the chunk carry a measured budget of its own so the move does not just relocate uncontrolled growth. A raise follows the same rule as max_bytes: a raise_log entry naming the chunk (`chunk`: this entry) and what was added.

Measured 209,890 bytes on 2026-10-20, with `yaml` external (inlined it is 472,201 — a second copy of the parser the dispatch bundle already carries). The ceiling is that reading plus about 10 %, rounded, because this chunk carries a 2,300-line concern plus the memory lookup and FTS index it reads, all of which still grow.

WHY IT WAS MOVED — AND THE REASON FIRST GIVEN WAS FALSE, which is recorded here rather than corrected silently. This entry said `chat-history` is bound on `session_start` and on no other event, and called it the largest narrow-event module the metafile ranks. An independent provider review of 2026-10-20 checked the manifest and refused the change on it: `chat-history` is bound on FIVE events — `session_start`, `session_end`, `stop`, `post_tool_use` and `user_prompt_submit` — across seven hosts. It is close to the widest-bound concern in the tree, not the narrowest. The claim came from reading the `session_start:` rows of the manifest and never the others.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, stated as narrowly as the evidence allows: the move takes 120,586 bytes out of a bundle every hook event parses (1,549,961 -> 1,429,414 B) and pays for them with one `require` of a 209,890-byte CJS file on the events that actually need the concern. Whether that is a latency WIN is UNMEASURED, and the 2026-10-18 council that chose this mechanism asked for exactly that proof inside `src/config/hook-latency-budget.json`. Until it exists this chunk is a byte-budget move with an unproven wall-clock effect, and the honest narrow-event candidates the same metafile ranks are recorded for whoever re-does it: `turn-end-gate` 71,928 B on `stop` alone, `injection-scan` 46,660 B on `post_tool_use` alone, `skill-route` 31,183 B and `git-authorization` 30,761 B on `user_prompt_submit` alone, `session-eol` 27,708 B on `stop` alone, `handoff-context` 25,220 B on `session_start` alone.

UNLIKE THE OTHER TWO CHUNKS this one carries a CONCERN, so there is a correct path behind the fast one: `_run_concern` tries the static registry, then `loadLazyConcern`, then the historical spawn-per-concern path. A missing or mis-digested chunk costs latency, never the concern's effect — which the same review confirmed, noting it holds because `src/scripts/` ships in the package.

Measured 11,097 bytes on 2026-10-23 (the observe-only `InstructionsLoaded` capture, its classifier, and the CLI entry the spawn fallback needs). The ceiling is that reading plus about 10 %, rounded, with no growth queued. Bound on `instructions_loaded` alone, so a chunk keeps it off every other dispatch's parse; the observer body ships here, never in the dispatch bundle. The binding that reaches it (one registry row and the event name in three vocabularies, 237 bytes) does sit in the bundle and is the 2026-10-23 raise of `max_bytes` recorded in `raise_log`. Like `chat_history` it carries a concern, so a missing chunk falls back to the spawn path and costs latency, never the capture.

chunks_note: A chunk is loaded only when a caller needs it, so its bytes are not paid by every dispatch; its ceiling exists so that the move out of dispatch.js stays a measured place rather than an unmeasured one. The gate builds each chunk with the exact esbuild segment `build:hook-chunks` uses for its entry.
max_yaml_packages_note: The dispatch path reads YAML for the hook manifest, the host-lowering table and the settings contract. One reader covers all three. Two cost 95,846 bytes for a single call site and were invisible until an external rescore counted them — which is why this is a cap rather than prose. The package set the cap counts over is YAML_PACKAGES in the gate.
what_this_does_not_bound: Latency. A smaller bundle is not a measured speed-up; src/config/hook-latency-budget.json owns the wall-clock axis and is not derived from this file. Nor does it bound dist/install/install.mjs or dist/mcp/server.mjs, which carry their own module graphs.
